channel.title: Pi Stack
channel.description: Comprehensive guides for open source alternatives, self-hosted software, privacy tools, and local AI deployment. Expert comparisons, setup guides, and benchmarks.

item.title: Drupal vs TYPO3 vs Joomla vs Contao in 2026: Which Enterprise CMS Should You Self-Host?
item.description: WordPress powers a huge slice of the public web, but it is the wrong tool the moment you need structured content, granular editorial permissions across hundreds of editors, audit trails, or a multi-site tree with per-language governance. That is exactly the gap where four battle-hardened PHP systems still dominate government, university, and manufacturing sites in 2026: Drupal, TYPO3, Joomla, and Contao.

item.title: gopls vs rust-analyzer vs clangd vs pyright in 2026: Which Language Server Actually Keeps Up?
item.description: Your editor feels slow and you blame the theme. It is almost never the theme. It is the language server: a background process that parses your repository, resolves types, and streams diagnostics over JSON-RPC. When it is healthy, go-to-definition is instant. When it is not, every keystroke queues behind a full re-index of a 400,000-line workspace.

item.title: Klipper vs Marlin vs RepRapFirmware in 2026: Which 3D Printer Firmware Should You Actually Flash?
item.description: Your printer’s mainboard is not the bottleneck. Its firmware is. A stock Ender 3 with Marlin and a stock Ender 3 running Klipper on a $15 Raspberry Pi are the same hardware with wildly different acceleration ceilings — and the difference shows up as ringing, corner bulge, and print time, not as a spec-sheet number.

item.title: Screego vs Neko vs Selkies in 2026: Which Self-Hosted Screen Sharing Stack Actually Works?
item.description: Sharing your screen should not require a corporate account, a 4-second delay between your cursor and your colleague’s monitor, or a subscription that bills per seat. Yet that is exactly what teams put up with every day — and it gets worse when the thing you need to share is not your laptop screen but an isolated browser session for testing a checkout flow, or a containerised desktop for a support engineer who is not allowed to install anything locally.

item.title: Self-Hosted Time & Attendance in 2026: OrangeHRM vs Anuko Time Tracker vs TimeTrex
item.description: Every payroll dispute starts the same way: someone claims they worked eight hours, the spreadsheet says seven and a half, and nobody can prove either number. Time and attendance software exists to make that argument impossible — a timestamped, auditable record of who was where, for how long, approved by a named supervisor.

item.title: Web Components in 2026: Lit vs FAST vs Stencil — Which Should You Actually Build On?
item.description: Every frontend team has a rewrite scar. The framework that felt inevitable five years ago is now a maintenance item, and the component library built on top of it is welded to a version that is no longer supported. Web Components are the one part of the browser platform that outlives the framework cycle: <status-badge> is a custom element today, in five years, and after the next three framework migrations.

item.title: DataFrames.jl vs TidierData.jl vs DataFramesMeta.jl in 2026: Which Julia Data Stack Should You Actually Use?
item.description: Julia’s pitch is that you never rewrite your prototype for production. That promise breaks the moment you pick a data manipulation layer, because the three serious options sit at completely different points between “R user comfort” and “compiler-friendly zero allocation” — and migrating between them rewrites 80% of your analysis code.

item.title: LVGL vs Slint vs Nuklear in 2026: Which Embedded GUI Toolkit Should You Actually Use?
item.description: Your device ships with a 320x240 display, 256 KB of RAM, and a project manager who wants the UI done yesterday. On the proprietary side, TouchGFX, emWin and Crank Storyboard all want per-seat licenses and NDA paperwork before you can read the docs. On the open side, three toolkits dominate every forum thread: LVGL, Slint and Nuklear. Picking wrong costs you months — a widget set that cannot fit your memory budget, or a project that stopped receiving commits in 2020.

item.title: PlatformIO vs ESP-IDF vs Arduino CLI in 2026: Which Embedded Build Toolchain Actually Ships Firmware Faster?
item.description: Three engineers on the same team flash three different boards, and none of their laptops can build anyone else’s firmware. That is the real cost of embedded toolchain choice in 2026 — not the compiler flags, but the fact that your build system decides who can reproduce your binary, and how fast CI can prove it.

item.title: Praat vs openSMILE vs audioFlux in 2026: Which Open-Source Speech Analysis Tool Actually Fits Your Research?
item.description: Speech researchers get squeezed from both sides. Commercial annotation suites quote per-seat prices that eat an entire grant line, while generic audio libraries give you a spectrogram and wish you luck with the rest. Three open tools cover almost every real workflow — Praat, openSMILE and audioFlux — but they were built for genuinely different jobs, and using the wrong one costs weeks.

item.title: PsychoPy vs jsPsych vs lab.js in 2026: Which Open-Source Platform Should Run Your Behavioral Experiment?
item.description: Every behavioral lab hits the same wall. The stimulus presentation software that defined the field — E-Prime, Presentation, SuperLab — is licensed per seat, per machine, and per year, and the licence rarely covers running participants online. Meanwhile half the subjects you need are at home with a laptop, not in your lab with a calibrated monitor.

item.title: Quarto vs R Markdown vs Bookdown in 2026: Which Reproducible Publishing Stack Should You Actually Use?
item.description: Every research group and platform team eventually hits the same wall: the analysis is reproducible, the document is not. Figures get pasted manually, the PDF drifts three revisions behind the notebook, and the person who knows which script generated table 4 left the company. Picking the wrong publishing stack means you rebuild that pipeline from scratch in eighteen months.

item.title: data.table vs dplyr vs tidytable in 2026: Which R Data Library Should You Actually Use?
item.description: An R script that reads a 4 GB CSV, groups by three columns and writes a summary should not take longer than your coffee break — but the same job can run in seconds or in minutes depending on which data library you load. That difference is not academic. It decides whether an analyst iterates five times an hour or twice a day, and it decides whether a laptop with 16 GB of RAM can hold the working set at all.

item.title: LittleFS vs SPIFFS vs FatFs in 2026: Which Embedded Filesystem Should You Actually Use?
item.description: Your firmware passed every test in the lab. Then a field unit loses power during a config write and comes back with an unreadable flash region — and suddenly your support queue is full of RMAs. On microcontrollers, the filesystem is not a detail you bolt on at the end. It is the component that decides whether a power cut corrupts your users’ data or is a non-event.

item.title: Mbed TLS vs wolfSSL vs BearSSL in 2026: Which Embedded TLS Stack Should You Ship?
item.description: A full TLS 1.3 handshake plus an X.509 chain validation path can eat more flash than your RTOS kernel and your application combined on a Cortex-M0+. On a 64 KB part with an internal radio stack already claiming half the budget, the choice between Mbed TLS, wolfSSL and BearSSL is not a library preference — it is a product decision that determines whether cloud connectivity, secure OTA and certificate rotation fit in the image at all.

item.title: MCUboot vs OpenBLT vs TinyUF2 in 2026: Secure Firmware Updates for Microcontrollers Compared
item.description: A product without a field update path has a maintenance model built on truck rolls. The moment a fleet of deployed devices needs a bug fix, the bootloader you chose two years earlier becomes the most expensive code in the project — and the one you can never change afterwards, because a failed bootloader update bricks hardware in the field.

item.title: PhpSpreadsheet vs League CSV vs ParseCsv in 2026: PHP CSV Parsing at Scale
item.description: Every PHP developer meets the same wall eventually: a customer uploads a 180 MB spreadsheet, your import job hits Allowed memory size of 512M exhausted, and the request dies halfway through a partially written database. The library you chose three years ago for its friendly array API is now the reason your nightly sync runs out of memory.

item.title: Rust on Microcontrollers in 2026: embedded-hal vs esp-hal vs rp-hal Compared
item.description: Embedded Rust stopped being an experiment the moment its interfaces stabilised. In 2026 the practical question is no longer “can I write firmware in Rust?” but “which HAL do I write my driver against, and what breaks when the silicon vendor changes it?” The three repositories that answer that question — embedded-hal, esp-hal and rp-hal — sit at different layers of the same stack, which is why comparing them as rivals misses the point and comparing them as collaborators is what actually ships products.

item.title: Java Terminal UI Libraries in 2026: JLine vs Lanterna vs Jansi
item.description: The most underrated deployment channel in 2026 is still SSH into a box and run something. Admin consoles, interactive installers, log browsers, Kafka lag dashboards rendered as text — all of it is Java-friendly, and all of it is a minefield the moment you need to read a keystroke, repaint a screen, or emit escape codes that survive Windows.

item.title: Kotlin CLI Frameworks in 2026: Clikt vs kotlinx-cli vs Mordant
item.description: Kotlin is a first-class server language, but its command-line story has quietly gone through a regime change. JetBrains’ own parser, kotlinx-cli, has not seen a commit since September 2023, while a community library called Clikt absorbed almost the entire ecosystem — 3,016 stars, multiplatform artifacts, and the kind of option-parsing ergonomics that make JVM startup feel worth it.
